title: An honest and good heart (Luke 8:4–21)
hookLine: the good soil keeps the word and bears fruit with patience

lines: THE WAITING IS THE HARD PART.
A SOWER WENT OUT TO SOW.
cards: A tomato seed goes into the ground. You water it and check it the next morning. Nothing.
A week later, a thin green thread. Weeks after that, maybe, something red. The waiting is the hard part.
A huge crowd has gathered from town after town, and Jesus tells them a story about exactly that. "A sower went out to sow his seed." Some lands on the path, trampled and eaten by birds.
Some on rock, where it sprouts and withers for lack of moisture. Some among thorns that choke it. And some on good ground, where it grows and bears a hundredfold.

teach.h: THE SEED IS THE WORD OF GOD.
teach.b: Jesus explains: "The seed is the word of God." The path is people who hear, but the word is snatched away. The rock is people who receive it with joy but have no root, and fall away when testing comes.
The thorns are people choked by "cares and riches and pleasures of this life." Then the good ground, with two details.
In the King James words: "But that on the good ground are they, which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience."
An honest and good heart: in Greek, kale kai agathe, a pairing some scholars say Greek writers used for a noble, upright person.
And with patience: hupomone, endurance; some readers unpack it as remaining under, staying put under a weight. The good soil isn't where things happen fast. It holds on through the season.
Then two short sayings. A lamp isn't lit to be put under a bed.
And: "Take heed therefore how ye hear." Not just what: how.
Finally, Jesus' mother and brothers arrive and can't reach him through the crowd, and he says: "My mother and my brethren are these which hear the word of God, and do it."
Some readers take that not as pushing his family away but as widening the circle; Luke has already shown Mary keeping words in her heart.

teach.h: KEEP IT, AND BRING FORTH FRUIT WITH PATIENCE.
teach.b: Hear and keep. Keep and do. Do, and wait.

how: The parable of the sower is often read in churches and used in Christian teaching as a way to reflect on how people hear and keep scripture over time.

o: a quick harvest that comes in a hundredfold
the good ground where a seed is planted
patience that endures, staying under a weight

games.q: what's inside Luke 8:4–21 — tap the pairs.
p: no root, falls away in testing

s: in Luke the good soil bears fruit quickly
Luke says it brings forth fruit with patience.
Jesus says to take heed how you hear
not only what you hear, but how.
Luke's sower explanation says "the seed is the word of God"

games.q: you've planted good seed. weeks pass and nothing shows. what does Luke's good soil do?
o: keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.
games.why: the good ground keeps the word and bears fruit with patience: hupomone, remaining under, holding on through the season.

practice: Think of something growing slowly in your life, a friendship you're rebuilding, someone else's recovery, maybe so slowly you doubt it's growing at all.
Picture it as a seed in late-winter ground, where the not-seeing is part of the process; breathe in, remaining under, and breathe out the need to see results today.
If you pray, you can ask for patience with slow things; if you don't, simply rest with the waiting.

wordCard.voice: Hupomone, Luke's Greek word for patience, endurance, staying under a weight: in the parable of the sower, the good soil is people who hear the word, keep it, and bear fruit with patience.

orig.note: Greek: patience, endurance. often explained as remaining under, staying put beneath a load.

carryVoice: Your line: bear fruit with patience. Good soil holds on through the whole season. Day five hundred thirty-one, done.
